summary:
Mars Navigator is an interactive, browser-based Martian survival map and mission-planning web application built with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. Designed around NASA planetary datasets—including MOLA topography, Viking surface imagery, and SHARAD subsurface water-ice models—the platform lets users explore Mars through switchable geospatial layers, evaluate potential landing zones, and plot multi-waypoint rover traverses.

The application directly addresses the challenge of human surface survival on Mars by turning complex orbital data into actionable mission logistics. Users can drop pins anywhere on the planet to generate real-time Habitat Suitability Scores based on safe Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) elevation, terrain slope, solar latitude, and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) water-ice access. Its route planner calculates spherical great-circle distances, elevation profiles, rover battery draw, and crew oxygen consumption.

Mars Navigator is important because it bridges the gap between raw space agency data and accessible public engagement. By framing planetary science as an interactive survival and engineering challenge, it empowers students, educators, and space enthusiasts to experience the real-world constraints of interplanetary exploration and settlement design.
details:
Here are the detailed specifications, design choices, and impact metrics for the Mars Navigator project:

1. What It Does & How It Works

Mars Navigator is an interactive, browser-based Martian surface map and mission-planning tool designed to simulate human settlement logistics on Mars.

  • How it works: It processes simulated NASA topography, atmospheric, and subsurface datasets (derived from MOLA, Viking, and SHARAD radar models) onto an interactive coordinate canvas. Users can switch between visual layers (elevation, surface imagery, water-ice deposits, and hazard slopes), click to drop landing site pins, plot multi-leg rove traverses, and instantly generate Areographic distance and elevation profiles.
  • The Survival Engine: Every coordinate clicked triggers a real-time Habitat Suitability Scoring algorithm that evaluates atmospheric braking safety (elevation), surface slope stability, solar availability (latitude), and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) water-ice proximity.

2. Benefits

  • Educational Interactivity: Translates complex planetary science into an intuitive, gamified exploratory format accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts.
  • Rapid Route Logistics: Allows mission planners and designers to visualize topography, calculate rover power draw, and gauge crew oxygen consumption across rough Martian terrain before deployment.
  • Zero-Install Accessibility: Built entirely for modern web standards, running seamlessly in any browser without needing heavy GIS desktop software.

3. Intended Impact

The project aims to bridge the gap between raw public planetary datasets and public engagement. By framing planetary science through the lens of human survival and exploration, it sparks curiosity in astrobiology, geospatial engineering, and interplanetary colonization logistics, inspiring the next generation of space systems designers.

4. Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Languages & Core Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and modern Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Data Visualization & Graphics: HTML5 Canvas API and SVG for rendering live topographic elevation profiles and responsive map overlays.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) with local preview servers, managed within a cloud-synced workspace.
  • Data Frameworks: Geometric great-circle calculations parameterized for Mars ($R_{\text{Mars}} = 3,389.5\text{ km}$) and multi-variable scoring heuristics simulating NASA design reference architectures.

5. Creative Elements

  • Mission-Control Aesthetic: Styled with high-tech HUD elements, live solar longitude ($L_s$) tracking, and dark-mode aerospace telemetry cards that evoke real NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) operations rooms.
  • Cross-Disciplinary Fusion: Combines serious geographical data visualization with game-like UI feedback, making cold scientific metrics (like hypsometric elevation models and hydrogen-equivalent water content) feel tactile and actionable.

6. Factors Considered During Development

  • Geospatial & Mathematical Precision: Ensuring spherical coordinate transformations and great-circle distance formulas account for Mars' equatorial radius and oblateness accurately.
  • UI/UX Performance: Optimizing canvas redraws and layer switching to maintain smooth 60fps panning and zooming without lag.
  • Survival Realism: Balancing playable interactivity with realistic constraints—such as weighting steep slopes and low-elevation atmospheric hazards heavily in the habitat suitability score.
